author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Government bond yields rose sharply and Asian stocks fell Friday as surging oil prices and stronger U.S. producer inflation increased expectations that major central banks may keep policy tighter.

In early Asian trading reported by Reuters, the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield reached 4.9708%, its highest level in about three years, while the 30-year yield rose to 5.3803%, a 19-year high. Futures markets put the chance of a Federal Reserve rate increase at roughly 70%. Those figures are snapshots from the article, not live quotes.

The selloff spread across regions. Japan’s Nikkei fell 2.8%, the CSI 300 dropped 1.2% and Hong Kong’s Hang Seng declined 1.5%. Australian three-year yields reached a 15-year high, while Japan’s 10-year yield approached 3%.

Energy was the central pressure point: Brent crude had climbed nearly 13% for the week after Middle East disruptions intensified supply concerns. Higher fuel costs can feed inflation while reducing household and business spending, a combination that complicates central-bank decisions and weighs on both bonds and equities.
dek: Government debt sold off and Asian equities fell after rising energy prices and U.S. producer inflation pushed investors toward tighter-rate expectations.
headline: Global bond yields surge as oil shock revives rate-hike bets
